name: Plovdiv
title: Holidays in Plovdiv
intro: A Roman theatre, colourful revival houses and a buzzing creative quarter in one of Europe's oldest cities. Here's what Plovdiv is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: A cobbled lane in Plovdiv's Old Town lined with white-walled revival houses with wooden balconies
facts_note: Bulgaria switched from the lev to the euro on 1 January 2026. The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June and September are ideal, warm enough for evenings outside without the heat of high summer. July and August often pass 30°C, so plan sightseeing for the morning and evening. Winters are cold and grey, but cheap and quiet.

things.name: Ancient Theatre
things.blurb: A Roman theatre carved into the hillside, still used for concerts and opera in summer.

things.name: Old Town
things.blurb: Steep cobbled lanes of brightly painted 19th-century merchant houses, several open as small museums.

things.name: Kapana
things.blurb: The creative quarter of narrow streets, with street art, craft shops, cafés and bars.

things.name: Roman Stadium
things.blurb: Part of a 2nd-century stadium is uncovered beneath the main shopping street, with seats you can sit on.

things.name: Nebet Tepe
things.blurb: A hilltop with ancient ruins and the best sunset view over the city's rooftops.

things.name: Bachkovo Monastery
things.blurb: One of Bulgaria's oldest monasteries, about half an hour south in the Rhodope Mountains.

faqs.question: Can you fly direct to Plovdiv from the UK?
faqs.answer: Yes, Ryanair has flown from London Stansted to Plovdiv, a little over three hours. Schedules change by season, and Sofia airport, about two hours away, has more flights.

faqs.question: Is Plovdiv worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It has Roman ruins, a pretty old town and a lively café scene, with prices well below most European cities.

faqs.question: What currency does Bulgaria use?
faqs.answer: The euro, since 1 January 2026. It replaced the Bulgarian lev.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Plovdiv?
faqs.answer: Two full days covers the main sights. Add a day for Bachkovo Monastery or the Rhodope Mountains.
